title: Phonon anomalies and critical scaling in the spin-$1/2$ trimer chain Na$_2$Cu$_3$Ge$_4$O$_{12}$
authors: P. Srikanth Patnaik, A. K. Bera, Srishti Bhardwaj, Tulika Maitra, Buddhananda Banerjee, Anushree Roy, S. M. Yusuf
abstract: Low-dimensional quantum magnets provide an ideal platform to explore spin-lattice coupling-mediated quantum correlations, which give rise to emergent quasiparticle excitations. The antiferromagnetically coupled spin-1/2 trimer chain of copper ions in Na$_2$Cu$_3$Ge$_4$O$_{12}$ (NCGO) hosts high-energy spin excitations of different species, whose energy scales overlap with those of lattice vibrations. Here, we report a comprehensive temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopic study performed between 80 and 400 K. The dynamic spin susceptibility, as obtained from the analysis of the broad spectral background, reveals the emergence of quasiparticle excitations below 170 K. We further identify an unusual crossover of phonon dynamics when the material transits from a normal paramagnetic state to a correlated quantum magnetic state. A power law dependence of the integrated Raman susceptibility of the phonon modes, $I_{χ^{\prime\prime}}^{i}\sim|T-T_{c}|^β$, is observed with the critical temperature $T_c$=167$\pm$1 K, and critical exponent $β= 0.24\pm 0.02$. The combined results obtained from the broad spectral background and sharp phonon peaks further indicate that the phonon renormalization observed across the crossover is driven by dynamic spin states. Additionally, statistical correlations among phonon energy eigenvalues, quantified through matrix-norm and power-test analyses of 200 spectra recorded at 80 K, reveal an unexpected linear correlation among phonon modes, also indicating that the collective lattice response is governed by spin correlations. These findings establish NCGO as a model system for investigating cooperative spin-lattice coupling and critical scaling behavior of phonon dynamics in low-dimensional magnetic materials.
summary: The authors used temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy on the magnetic material $	ext{Na}_2	ext{Cu}_3	ext{Ge}_4	ext{O}_{12}$ to study spin-lattice coupling. They found a critical scaling behavior near $T_c \approx 167$ K, demonstrating that phonon anomalies are directly governed by the underlying dynamic spin correlations. This establishes NCGO as an excellent model for studying cooperative quantum phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates spin-lattice coupling-mediated quantum correlations and critical scaling behavior of phonon dynamics in low-dimensional magnetic materials.
main_result: The research found evidence that the phonon renormalization across a magnetic crossover is driven by dynamic spin states, establishing the material as a model system for cooperative spin–lattice coupling.
method: Temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy was used to measure both sharp phonon peaks and broad spectral backgrounds related to spin excitations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the antiferromagnetically coupled spin-$1/2$ trimer chain $	ext{Na}_2	ext{Cu}_3	ext{Ge}_4	ext{O}_{12}$ (NCGO). The structure involves a zigzag arrangement of copper trimers.
key_observables: Dynamic spin susceptibility ($\chi''$) from the background spectrum, phonon integral intensity ($I_i$), and critical exponents ($ eta$).
important_parameters: $T_c = 167 \pm 1 	ext{ K}$ (critical temperature) and $ eta = 0.24 \pm 0.02$ (critical exponent). Measurements span from 80 K to 400 K.
main_assumptions: Interchain interactions are assumed weak; the analysis relies on fitting the Raman response function with phonon Lorentzians and a background term for spin excitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, schematic of exchange couplings, and show temperature-dependent Raman spectra used to extract both sharp phonon modes and broad spectral backgrounds related to spin dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the material's magnetic and structural properties using DFT calculations, followed by detailed temperature-dependent Raman measurements. Key analyses include fitting the background for dynamic susceptibility and analyzing power-law scaling of phonon intensities near the critical point.
why_interesting: This work directly links lattice dynamics (phonons) to electronic/magnetic correlations (spin excitations), which is a core topic in understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated quantum materials relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems modeling.
